title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the sequel of 'La Longue Marche', on the 'équation des lacets'. pi_{0,3} is the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. It is generated by the loops l_0, l_1, l_infinity, subject to l_0 l_1 l_infinity = 1. The symmetric group S_3 acts on it by permuting 0, 1, infinity. sigma_infinity is the involution exchanging 0 and 1. rho is the order-3 rotation; the same letter rho is also used for the cyclotomic exponent in hat-Z^*.

Previous page. Grothendieck redoes computations from his earlier notes [C]. He considers outer automorphisms of hat-pi_{0,3} that commute with S_3. Each can be lifted uniquely to a genuine automorphism u that commutes with sigma_infinity and commutes with rho up to an inner automorphism. Such u correspond bijectively to pairs (g_0 mod L_0, rho in hat-Z^*). These pairs must satisfy:
- (9) and (10): a 2-cycle relation and a hexagon-type relation, written in terms of h_0 = [sigma_infinity, g_0^{-1}];
- (10 bis): an order-3 cocycle condition, with gamma = (rho-1)/2.
This is exactly the shape of Drinfeld's GT (lambda, f), with gamma playing the role of m = (lambda-1)/2 and h_0 in the role of f.

This page, formula (11). u is written explicitly on the generators:
- u(l_0) = int(g_0)(l_0^rho);
- u(l_1) = int(sigma_infinity(g_0))(l_1^rho);
- u(l_infinity) is a conjugate of l_infinity^rho.

This page, (11 bis). Strictly speaking, beyond (9) and (10), one must also require that u(l_0) and u(l_1) generate hat-pi_{0,3}. In modern terms this is the condition separating the monoid underline-GT from the group GT, i.e. invertibility.

The extended group. Grothendieck then extends u to hat-G^+_{0,3}, the extension of S_3 by hat-pi_{0,3}. This is the profinite completion of the orbifold fundamental group of the quotient (P^1 minus three points)/S_3, i.e. of the j-line. It is generated by l'_1 = sigma_infinity and l'_infinity = rho^{-1}, which gives hat-PSL_2(Z) = hat(Z/2 * Z/3), containing pi_{0,3} as a normal subgroup of index 6 (the image of Gamma(2)).
- (13): u sigma_infinity u^{-1} = sigma_infinity, by construction.
- (14): rho^{-1} u rho = int(h) u, with h = (rho^{-1} sigma_infinity)(g_0) l_0^gamma g_0^{-1}. Equivalently u rho u^{-1} = int(rho(h)) rho, with rho(h) = sigma_infinity(g_0) l_1^gamma rho(g_0)^{-1}.
- (15): u(sigma_infinity) = sigma_infinity and u(rho) = g rho, with g = sigma_infinity(g_0) l_1^gamma rho(g_0)^{-1}.

Next page. The relation sigma^2 = 1 is preserved trivially. The relation rho^3 = 1 reduces to g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1, which follows from (10). This is the familiar description of the GT (and Galois) action on the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) / the orbifold pi_1 of M_{1,1}.
errors: The formula for u(l_infinity) in (11) is hard to read and appears to contain a slip: an exponent written as '-sigma' where gamma, or a sign of gamma, is presumably meant. It cannot be fully checked from the image.

The letter rho is overloaded: it denotes both the order-3 automorphism and the element of hat-Z^* used as an exponent (l_0^rho). Expressions such as rho^{-1}(h_0) versus l_0^rho must be read according to context.
The step from (14) to (15) is stated as 'on vérifie' without any computation; it is consistent in form, but the verification is not written out.

ideas.what: Parametrising automorphisms of hat-pi_{0,3} that commute with S_3 by pairs (g_0, rho in hat-Z^*), subject to a 2-cycle, a hexagon, and an order-3 condition, with gamma = (rho-1)/2
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group hat-GT (two- and three-cycle relations)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme states the program (Teichmüller tower, generators and relations in genus 0 and 1) but not these formulas

ideas.what: The extra requirement that u(l_0), u(l_1) generate the group (invertibility)
ideas.modern_name: Passage from the monoid underline-GT to the group GT

ideas.what: Extension of the action to hat-G^+_{0,3} = hat(Z/2 * Z/3) = hat-PSL_2(Z): sigma fixed, rho sent to g rho with g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1
ideas.modern_name: GT / Galois action on the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) (orbifold pi_1 of M_{1,1} / Teichmüller group Gamma_{1,1})

missed.claim: This is an independent, explicit derivation of the action of GT-type automorphisms on hat-PSL_2(Z), extended from pi_{0,3} via the S_3 symmetry. It predates or parallels Lochak–Schneps. It is historically relevant as part of Grothendieck's own early GT computations, but the result itself is known.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's priority and his concrete route (via the extension of S_3 by pi_{0,3}) to the genus-0 to genus-1 link in the Teichmüller tower. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out explicit early computations of what is now Drinfeld's GT acting on hat-PSL_2(Z). This is historically interesting, but the mathematics is fully known (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps), and the page contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'en considérant le groupe commun engendré' should read 'en considérant ce groupe comme engendré'.
'forment des généra-lisateurs' should read 'forment des générateurs'.
'int(u_0).\sigma_\infty' is most likely 'int(u).\sigma_\infty' (inner action of u inside the holomorph).
In (11), the third line's exponent written '-\sigma' is likely '-\gamma' (illegible).
